incidents.victim: US, Ukrainian and European officials, military and journalists
incidents.vector: Social-engineering phishing posing as messaging-app support staff to trick high-value targets into surrendering verification codes, PINs and backup recovery keys for Signal, WhatsApp and similar apps.
incidents.impact: FBI/CISA and Ukraine's SBU say Russian intelligence clusters have hijacked individual encrypted-messaging accounts to read historical and group messages; the campaign is ongoing with newly evolved tactics targeting backup recovery keys.

incidents.vector: Phishing emails carrying malicious Remote Desktop Protocol configuration files that deploy the newly documented StockStay malware, disguised as PDF readers and calculator apps.
incidents.impact: Google reports Russia's long-running Turla group has run a parallel espionage toolkit (StockStay, modeled on its older Kazuar framework) against Ukrainian and European government and defense targets since 2022, ensuring persistent access even as tools are discovered.

incidents.victim: John Bolton (former US National Security Advisor)
incidents.vector: Compromise of a personal email account that Bolton had used to store and transmit classified 'diary' notes after leaving office.
incidents.impact: DOJ disclosed, alongside Bolton's guilty plea to retaining national defense information, that an Iran-linked actor hacked his personal email and accessed top-secret material; Bolton reported the hack but did not disclose the account held national defense information.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-day (CVE-2026-20245) via a malicious CSV tenant upload, after rogue peering connections and SSH access, to create a hidden root account ('troot').
incidents.impact: Mandiant says the attacker gained root-level control of the provider's SD-WAN orchestrator earlier in 2026, potentially exposing all internal corporate traffic; extensive anti-forensic cleanup left the full scope unclear. Cisco has since patched the flaw.

incidents.vector: Breach of a third-party vendor that managed the intelligence agency's mobile device management platform, linked to a wave of attacks against Ivanti EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence officers, exposing sensitive personnel details of the country's state security service.

incidents.victim: Transport for London; SSM Health and Sutter Health (US)
incidents.vector: Social engineering, SIM-swapping and SMS/voice phishing to steal employee credentials and bypass multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Two UK members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty over the August 2024 attack that crippled Transport for London and (for one defendant) intrusions at US healthcare providers; the wider group is tied to 120 intrusions and at least $115M in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and bulk data theft, with the stolen files listed on the group's extortion leak site.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a breach after the World Leaks group claimed it stole more than 200,000 documents, allegedly including sensitive data on Apple and Tesla electronic components.

incidents.victim: Klue customers — LastPass, Snyk and other firms
incidents.vector: Compromise of a legacy integration credential at market-analytics platform Klue, then theft of customers' OAuth tokens to pivot into their connected Salesforce instances and download data.
incidents.impact: At least eight companies, including LastPass and Snyk, confirmed data stolen from their Salesforce accounts via the Klue breach; a group calling itself Icarus is extorting victims and the list is expected to grow.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of FortiSandbox flaws (CVE-2026-39808 OS-command injection and CVE-2026-39813 path traversal, plus CVE-2026-25089) to bypass authentication, escalate privileges and run arbitrary commands.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed dozens of exploitation events from multiple sources against the security appliance; post-exploitation reconnaissance suggests early stages of a broader wave against the trusted sandbox systems that connect to other Fortinet devices.

incidents.victim: US and Canadian medical, academic and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploitation of externally facing REDCap research servers, deployment of custom INFINITERED malware to harvest credentials, then abuse of enterprise domain-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive email.
incidents.impact: Google attributes a campaign undetected since September 2023 to China-nexus group UNC6508, which targeted defense, AI, medical and national-security research; Google disrupted infrastructure but assesses the actor remains active and known victims are likely a fraction of the total.

incidents.victim: Universities, Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar, Kodak
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft ERP zero-day to steal data, followed by extortion via a dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters group has been exploiting an Oracle PeopleSoft flaw since late May to compromise and extort a growing roster of universities and major corporations; many listed victims have confirmed breaches.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to parts of the company's internal network, with sensitive data copied before detection.
incidents.impact: The Danish pharma giant behind Ozempic and Wegovy disclosed an intrusion in which some sensitive data, including patient personal information, was copied; affected systems were taken offline to evict the attackers.

incidents.victim: Awesome Motive WordPress plugin users (~1.2M websites)
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise injecting malicious JavaScript into legitimate updates of the OptinMonster, TrustPulse and PushEngage plugins, which create hidden admin accounts and a self-concealing backdoor when a site admin logs in.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million WordPress websites were backdoored through the compromised plugins, giving attackers persistent administrative access.

incidents.victim: Major Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, EDBI)
incidents.vector: Attack on shared communications infrastructure used by the four banks, knocking out their online portals and mobile apps.
incidents.impact: A cyberattack disrupted services at four of Iran's largest banks over a weekend; intelligence sources believe Israeli hackers were likely responsible. The banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Abuse of the Arch User Repository 'orphaned package' adoption mechanism to take over more than 1,900 abandoned packages and add install steps that pull a rootkit and credential-stealing infostealer.
incidents.impact: A large-scale supply-chain attack hijacked roughly 1,900 community Arch Linux packages to deploy a rootkit and infostealer capable of harvesting browser credentials, developer secrets and access keys before maintainers intervened.

incidents.vector: Mass internet scanning and password spraying against FortiGate, Sophos, Citrix and MSSQL services, exploitation of unpatched flaws, a custom 'FortigateSniffer' to intercept credentials, and a 45-GPU cluster to crack hashes offline.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' campaign exposed valid admin and VPN credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate firewalls across 194 countries, with confirmed compromises in government, finance and critical infrastructure; a Turkish NATO defense contractor allegedly had classified documents exfiltrated. The Russian-speaking broker remains active and sells the access on.
